review_comments.body:
**Remapped Control stays pressed** If Linux maps physical Alt to logical Control, `releasedModifier(LogicalKeyboardKey.controlLeft, PhysicalKeyboardKey.altLeft)` returns `alt` before reaching the Control check. Key-down sets `ctrl` from `e.isControlPressed`, but key-up clears `alt` instead. This leaves `ctrl` set, so later mouse clicks can act like Control-clicks. Check all recognized logical modifiers first, then fall back to the physical key when the logical key is not a modifier.
Prompt To Fix With AI `````markdown This is a comment left during a code review. Path: flutter/lib/models/input_modifier_utils.dart Line: 212-216 Comment: **Remapped Control stays pressed** If Linux maps physical Alt to logical Control, `releasedModifier(LogicalKeyboardKey.controlLeft, PhysicalKeyboardKey.altLeft)` returns `alt` before reaching the Control check. Key-down sets `ctrl` from `e.isControlPressed`, but key-up clears `alt` instead. This leaves `ctrl` set, so later mouse clicks can act like Control-clicks. Check all recognized logical modifiers first, then fall back to the physical key when the logical key is not a modifier. --- For each issue above, determine whether it is valid and should be fixed. If so, fix it directly. `````

** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Prefer a recognized logical modifier over a conflicting physical modifier.** With XKB `ctrl:swap_lalt_lctl`, a physical left Alt key can report logical Control. `releasedModifier` returns `ModifierKind.alt` for that release. The raw key-up handler then leaves its cached `ctrl` flag set, so later remote input can carry `ctrl=true`. Check recognized logical modifiers first. Use the physical key when the logical key is not a modifier, as in the group-switch case. ([manpages.debian.org](https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/xkb-data/xkeyboard-config.7.en.html?utm_source=openai))
